title: IBM's CP-40 and the 1960s Invention of the Virtual Machine
explainer: Long before 'the cloud,' IBM researchers at the Cambridge Scientific Center built CP-40 in the mid-1960s, giving each timesharing user what felt like a private, fully isolated computer running on shared hardware; the approach matured into the commercial VM/370 system IBM announced in 1972. Every modern cloud platform you deploy a container to is a direct descendant of that original insight: one physical machine can safely host many isolated, independently managed 'computers.' Seeing this origin makes clear that cloud elasticity is an old idea - resource-sharing through isolation - delivered through much newer tooling.
